content:
A data lakehouse combines the best elements of a data lake and a data warehouse. Data lakes are systems or repositories of data, stored in their natural/raw format, which can handle a wide range of analytics from batch to machine learning. On the other hand, data warehouses provide a storage system for data that has already been processed and transformed, with a more efficient way to do analytical processing.

The difference between a data lakehouse and a data warehouse lies primarily in how they handle data. While a data warehouse deals with structured and processed data, a data lakehouse can manage both raw (unstructured/semi-structured) and structured data. It provides cost-effective, flexible data storage, and also maintains the performance, reliability, and data quality features of data warehouse systems. Therefore, a lakehouse represents a new, open paradigm that combines the best elements of data lakes and data warehouses.
